mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 2.5% in a given month coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in a month
failure_condition: Over 60-day window, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite trigger, or Fed Funds stays above 2.5% for >3 consecutive months with no negative SPX 20d returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE by at least 0.2 percentage points is associated with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-market tightness reduces recession risk.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by ≥0.2pp in a month
failure_condition: In 20-day windows following UNRATE up-moves ≥0.2pp, SPX 20d returns are not statistically different from the prior month's average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in GDPC1 (real private demand) exceeding 2% of the prior month's value predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals sustained economic momentum.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon following the trigger, cumulative SPX 20d returns are negative or the 60-day IC is below 0.05 versus the pre-trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both INDPRO (industrial production) and HOUST (housing starts) by at least 1% each, relative to the prior month, predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals softening supply-side conditions.
failure_condition: In 20-day windows after the trigger, SPX 20d returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or INDPRO recovers >1% within 2 months while HOUST remains depressed.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.5 percentage points in a month during a non-inflationary regime, the S&P 500 exhibits a negative 60-day forward return due to higher real interest rates compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS ↑ >0.5pp in a month AND inflation < 3% (CPIAUCSL < 105)
failure_condition: Over 60 days post-trigger, SPX 20d returns are not persistently negative across 5 such events, or inflation rises >3% within the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in PAYEMS (employment months) by at least 2,000 since the last peak is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as rising labor market slack increases recession risk.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS month-over-month decline ≥2,000 since last monthly peak
failure_condition: In triggered windows, SPX 20d returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05), or PAYEMS recovers to prior peak within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in RSAFS (real household spending) by at least 1% signals a demand shock that is expected to produce a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investors anticipate weaker earnings.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS month-over-month ↓1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 20 days after the trigger, SPX 20d returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or RSAFS recovers >1% in the third month.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and GDPC1 fall simultaneously by at least 1% in a month, the S&P 500 shows a positive 5-day forward return as the dual softness reduces recession probability and supports risk-on sentiment.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO ↓1% AND GDPC1 ↓1% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual soft supply and demand indicators
failure_condition: Within 5 days post-trigger, SPX 20d returns are not positive (p > 0.05), or one of the proxies recovers >1% within 2 days.
